key_insight: Layer choice matters: adapting only the most sensitivity-matched Transformer layers can improve target-task performance while preserving more general LLM capabilities.
engineering_relevance: LS-LoRA offers a simple, forward-only way to place LoRA adapters more efficiently, reducing capability loss without adding replay data or explicit regularization.
method: Estimate layer sensitivity with input-output cosine similarity as a lightweight proxy for empirical Fisher information.
Select low-similarity layers as adaptation sites.
Insert trainable LoRA adapters only in those layers (LS-LoRA).
evidence_signal: Across models and tasks in mathematical reasoning and code generation, low input-output similarity layers aligned with higher Fisher scores and LS-LoRA outperformed standard all-layer LoRA on target performance while retaining more commonsense reasoning.
watch_item: The proxy-guided layer ranking may depend on model and task, so sensitivity selection should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: Where to Adapt Matters: Layer-Selective Fine-Tuning for Capability Retention
